records.issue_text: Email comparison is case-sensitive in uniqueGuests filter allowing duplicate attendee rows via createMany
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees using a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist check `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not). Because neither side is normalized (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`), `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com` will be treated as different and can pass the filter, then be inserted via `attendees.createMany` without `skipDuplicates`, allowing duplicate attendee rows differing only by email casing.

records.issue_text: In sendAddGuestsEmails, newGuests.includes(attendee.email) case-sensitivity sends wrong email type for case-differing guests
records.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the branch `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) { ... }` uses `Array.prototype.includes`, which is case-sensitive. In this diff, guest emails are never normalized (e.g., lowercased) before being stored/compared: the handler passes raw `guests` input to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` and filtering uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` as well. Therefore, if a guest is added as `Foo@Example.com` but `attendee.email` is `foo@example.com` (or vice versa), the `includes` check will fail and the wrong email template will be sent for that attendee.
